messages:
laura_sales: Hey team — ACME POC is hitting 403s on the /v1/generate endpoint and occasional 429s. They sent this curl that fails. Can we swarm?

laura_sales: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer poc_key_abc123' \\n  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: acme-org' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}'```

laura_sales: Response: `{\"error\":\"permission_denied\",\"message\":\"key not bound to project\"}` and sometimes `{"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":3}`.

mike_se: Ugh. Did they create a service key scoped to the right project? Ask them to confirm the key type (API key vs POC key) and the org/project headers.

mike_se: Can you paste the exact request headers from their logs (no secrets except the header names)?

ashley_sre: I can check our auth logs for that key ID. @deploy-bot can you fetch recent auth failures for key prefix `poc_key_abc` across the last 10 minutes?

deploy-bot: Fetching auth events for key prefix "poc_key_abc" from 2112344678..2112345878. Found 18 events — 14 permission_denied (project-binding), 4 rate_limited. Returning redacted snippets.

ashley_sre: Snippet from our side: `AUTH FAIL key=poc_key_abc... reason=project-missing tenant=acme-org request=/v1/generate ip=34.122.11.9`

laura_sales: I asked ACME and they say they set X-Redwood-Org: acme-org and didn't set X-Redwood-Project. They thought org-level keys were enough.

mike_se: That's the issue. For POC keys in our sandbox, keys must be bound to a project. If no X-Redwood-Project header, the runtime rejects with 403. Quick workaround: have them include `X-Redwood-Project: acme-poc` in the request.

mike_se: Example header: `-H 'X-Redwood-Project: acme-poc'`

laura_sales: They tried that and still hit 403 once. Sent this log: `permission_denied: key bound to different project`

ashley_sre: That suggests the key is bound to a different project or tenant binding mismatch. I'll look up the key binding in the control plane. Give me 3m.

ashley_sre: Control plane: key=poc_key_abc123 bound_org=acme-org bound_project=acme-poc-2 key_type=service_account scopes=[generate,embeddings]

ashley_sre: So the key is bound to `acme-poc-2` but ACME tried `acme-poc`. That will 403.

mike_se: Ok — options: 1) update the header to use acme-poc-2, 2) rebind the key to acme-poc (requires a rotate), or 3) create a new key bound to acme-poc. For a fast POC, have them use the exact project name in the header.

laura_sales: I told ACME to use `X-Redwood-Project: acme-poc-2`. They confirm now they get a 200 for normal requests. Still seeing occasional 429s during a stress test.

ashley_sre: 429s during load look like they hit the per-key TPS quota in sandbox. The auth events show bursts — retry_after=3 for most. We can increase their burst quota temporarily for the demo.

mike_se: I'll authorize a temporary bump for the demo window. @ashley_sre can you apply a +50 TPS burst for 1 hour to key=poc_key_abc123?

ashley_sre: On it. Patch applied: sandbox_quota.bump key=poc_key_abc123 delta=+50 duration=1h. Monitor and revert at 2112349488.

laura_sales: ACME reran stress, no 429s now, 200s all around. Thanks team!

dan_security: Two notes: 1) we should remind sales to avoid sharing full keys in screenshots (redacted above, 👍). 2) For enterprise POCs, add a doc blurb about project vs org binding and key types — saves time.

mike_se: Agreed. I'll add a short FAQ in the sales POC checklist. Also opening an internal docs ticket to clarify error message text when key/project mismatch happens.

laura_sales: Filed follow-up: ENG-5678 docs update + generate clearer 403 message. ACME is green for the demo. Closing swarm. :tada:
